sites.ownership: The application controller owns shared multi-window lifecycle state.
sites.justification: App actions and lifecycle signals route to the last-focused editor window and maintain a window registry without global statics.

sites.ownership: GTK tests reuse the shared application-state container.
sites.justification: The test harness drives the same window routing and activation paths as runtime code, including last-focused resolution.

sites.ownership: The test-only window helper borrows shared application state.
sites.justification: Tests need controlled access to the window registry without introducing a second window-lifecycle path.

sites.ownership: App-scoped actions borrow shared application state.
sites.justification: New, new-window, open, open-folder, and recent-open actions must reuse the last-focused editor window or create a new one exactly once.

sites.ownership: File actions borrow shared application state.
sites.justification: File actions need window routing that preserves window-local tabs and compare state while allowing new windows to start empty.

sites.ownership: App actions borrow shared application state.
sites.justification: Preferences/help/about actions need a stable editor window target so dialogs do not attach to non-editor transient windows.

sites.ownership: Application lifecycle callbacks borrow shared application state.
sites.justification: Activation and open signals must share the session-restore gate and resolve the correct editor window when multiple windows exist.

sites.ownership: Window resolution borrows shared application state.
sites.justification: Window creation is centralized so the registry and last-focused tracking remain consistent across action and lifecycle entry points.

sites.ownership: Active editor window resolution reads shared application state.
sites.justification: Window routing prefers the last-focused editor window while still allowing a deterministic fallback when focus tracking is unavailable.

sites.ownership: Window creation borrows shared application state.
sites.justification: New windows register destroy/focus handlers that update the shared registry without leaking strong reference cycles.

sites.ownership: Tab-transfer window handler borrows shared application state.
sites.justification: Moving a tab to a new window must create a registered secondary editor window through the same lifecycle registry as normal window creation.

sites.ownership: Window registration mutates shared application state.
sites.justification: Destroy and focus notifications must add/remove windows and update last-focused tracking to keep action routing correct.
